kicker: In a gold rush, the shovel sellers get rich first.
summary: Every question you type runs on someone's chip — and the money flowing around those chips is shaping the whole AI industry.

quiz.q: Rivals already have powerful chips. Why is NVIDIA still hard to beat?
options: NVIDIA chips are the cheapest on the market
The whole industry is used to writing software on CUDA
The law bans chips from other makers
Other makers' chips cannot run AI
quiz.explain: NVIDIA's moat is CUDA, a software platform dating from 2006. Switching to another chip means rewriting or converting a great deal of code.

gardeners.label: A thousand gardeners
gardeners.art: A terraced hill like a bonsai tray under a low full moon: 25 curved rows of 40 moss beds each, a bamboo gutter along every lip with a little spout over every bed. Front left, a paper gardener stands on a stepping stone by a stone lantern, his watering can on a rock beside him; on the crest, the bamboo valve at the head of the gutters meets the spring.
gardeners.hint: Drag to turn the tray. Touch the watering can, or the bamboo valve on the crest.
gardeners.group: Two ways to water the same garden
gardeners.oneAria: Water with one can: a few strong cores doing one job after another
gardeners.manyAria: Water with a thousand bamboo spouts: thousands of small cores working at once

insight.text: A GPU (graphics processor) is like a thousand gardeners watering at once: just right for AI's billions of tiny sums.

gardeners.detail: CPUs are still needed to coordinate and make decisions. A neural network, though, mostly multiplies and adds huge tables of numbers, work that splits neatly into parallel pieces.

scaling.label: Growing takes more shovels
scaling.art: A three-cornered stone basin on a mossy boulder, seen from a little above; each corner spills into a jar: Data front left, Size at the back, Compute front right. A bamboo spout resting on a single post lets a thread of silver drops fall into the middle, where a sapling stands on a small stone against the moon. Behind the mist, an old tree with a great trunk waits.
scaling.basinAria: The three-cornered stone basin: drag it, or use the arrow keys, to tilt it toward a corner

jars.name: Data
jars.aria: Data jar: how much text the model reads

jars.name: Size
jars.aria: Size jar: the model's number of parameters

jars.name: Compute
jars.aria: Compute jar: chips and hours of running

scaling.lopsided: The tree leans: the {name} jar is low

insights.text: Scaling laws: add data, size and compute, and a model improves steadily and predictably.
In 2022 Chinchilla (70 billion parameters, 1.4 trillion tokens) beat Gopher, four times its size: balancing data with size pays off.

scaling.detail: Because the curve is so steady, many companies believe more chips mean better models — so they keep buying chips.

moat.label: The moat round the castle
moat.art: Seen from high above, a round disc floating in the night: in the middle, a three-roofed stone castle on its island; round it, a black moat crossed by six hundred little bamboo bridges from a village of low roofs. On the far lake, three boats with paper lanterns (round, tall, square) wait by three canals.
moat.boatAria: {name} boat: see what this rival is doing

fact.text: Oct 2025: Anthropic announced it will use up to a million Google TPU chips, over 1 gigawatt of capacity in 2026.
Feb 2026: in its new funding round, OpenAI agreed to use 2 gigawatts of compute running on Amazon's Trainium chips.
Oct 2025: AMD and OpenAI signed a 6-gigawatt GPU deal; the first gigawatt (MI450) starts in the second half of 2026.

insight.text: NVIDIA's moat is CUDA: a software platform from 2006 that the whole industry is used to writing code on.

detail.text: Some big AI labs use several kinds of chip side by side: Anthropic says it uses TPUs, Trainium and NVIDIA GPUs.

goldrush.label: Gold-rush season
goldrush.art: A long black ridge cut from paper runs across the lower part, a giant moon behind it that you drag through the seasons. Each milestone is a lamp post on the ridge; diggers with lanterns climb in ever greater numbers toward the shovel seller's tent on the summit, where two heaps of gold stand in true proportion.
goldrush.prompt: Drag the moon through the seasons
goldrush.sliderAria: Drag the moon through NVIDIA's milestones

fact.text: NVIDIA introduces CUDA: a way to use GPUs for any calculation, not just drawing game graphics.
Kaplan's team (OpenAI) shows that bigger models with more data and compute make fewer word-prediction errors, along a smooth curve.
In the fiscal year ending January 2023, NVIDIA's data-centre business brought in $15.0 billion.
NVIDIA becomes the first company worth more than $5 trillion on the stock market.
In fiscal 2026 data centres brought in $193.7 billion, nearly 13 times the figure three years earlier.
Latest report (26 Aug 2026): data centres earned $89 billion in one quarter, up 117% on a year earlier.

horizon.text: Some investors predict NVIDIA will be the first $10 trillion company; nobody knows how long the boom will last.

insight.text: About 9 in 10 dollars of NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 revenue came from data centres: the shovel seller gets paid first.

loop.label: The money loop
loop.art: Looking up from below the axle at a great wooden waterwheel beside NVIDIA's stone mill, against the moon. A stone flume carries water from the wheel's tail round the lake past the AI company's island (a pavilion with a lamp) and the data centre's (a row of stone lanterns), then over the mill roof back onto the wheel; the mill wall bears two notches, 22 and 51.
loop.wheelAria: The waterwheel: drag it round its axle, or press the right arrow or Enter, to turn it a quarter
flow: NVIDIA invests in an AI company
The AI company builds data centres
The data centres buy NVIDIA chips
NVIDIA's revenue rises, so it has more to invest

facts.text: Feb 2026: NVIDIA put $30 billion into OpenAI's $110 billion funding round, alongside Amazon and SoftBank.
NVIDIA's stakes in private companies grew from $22 billion to $51 billion in just the first six months of 2026.
Aug 2026: NVIDIA guaranteed up to $105 billion for building data centres that serve an OpenAI subsidiary.

view.text: These deals sit “right in the middle” of the circular-investment debate, but if they work they could become a competitive moat.
NVIDIA weighing a guarantee for OpenAI adds strain to the already contested story of “the supplier funding its customer”.
NVIDIA's money is only part of what customers must raise; he calls the “circular” charge groundless.
Oct 2025: share prices, especially of AI-focused tech companies, look stretched; the risk of a sharp market correction has risen.

common.text: Everyone sees money circling between NVIDIA and its customers; they differ on whether it is a moat or the seed of a bubble.

insight.text: NVIDIA invests in the very customers who buy its chips: moat or bubble, analysts still disagree.
